author: FS-GG
name: FS.GG Governance overlay
description: Drops the pinned FS.GG.Governance reference gate set into an existing SDD-managed project to activate Governance. Ships build, test, evidence, command-free gameplay floors, controlled-import verification, and schema generations; non-blocking by default (light).

sources.//: This template had NO `sources` block, and that was not the safe default it looked like (FS.GG.Templates#386). Declaring `exclude` REPLACES the engine's list wholesale, so the four workspace templates restate it and this one inherited it — and the inherited list does NOT exclude `node_modules/` or `.nuget/`. MEASURED, not read: a folder install of this template with both directories seeded delivered BOTH into the generated product. The engine's real defaults, measured on dotnet SDK 10.0.302 by instantiating a template that declares no `sources` block at all and seeding one file per pattern at two depths, are the six restated below — `bin`, `obj`, `.template.config`, `*.filelist`, `*.user`, `*.lock.json` were filtered at both depths; `node_modules/` was DELIVERED at both depths. The `strings -el` reading that put `**/node_modules/**` among the defaults is a false positive: the string sits adjacent to them in the binary's string pool, not in the effective list. Unlike its four siblings this list KEEPS `**/*.lock.json`, because this is an overlay that ships no lockfiles and #380's reason to drop it does not apply here — the only thing this block changes about how this template behaves is that the two directories below can no longer reach a product.

appName.description: Project/solution name used in the governed command strings (e.g. 'dotnet build <App>.slnx') and the governance project id.

defaultProfile.description: Default Governance profile. 'light' is the deliberate non-blocking inner-loop posture; switch to 'strict'/'release' to make the block-on-ship gates block at Verify.

choices.description: Tightens the blocking floor to Verify.
